entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sosibius of Tarentum was a Tarentine from Magna Graecia, one of the captains of the body-guards of Ptolemy Philadelphus, king of Egypt. He played a significant role in the protection of Ptolemy's court and was possibly the father of Sosibius, minister of Ptolemy Philopator.

Sosibius's involvement in the Egyptian royal court was likely a result of the growing influence of Magna Graecia in the Mediterranean during the 4th century BCE. This period saw the rise of Greek cities in the eastern Mediterranean, which became major centers of power and culture.

The legacy of Sosibius of Tarentum can be seen in the continuation of Greek cultural and political traditions in the Mediterranean after the fall of the Ptolemaic Kingdom. His descendants, including the minister Sosibius, continued to play important roles in the politics and society of the region.

The impact of Sosibius of Tarentum's life and career can be measured in the enduring legacy of Greek culture in the Mediterranean, which continues to shape the art, literature, and politics of the region to this day.
